design_brief:
**BrailleGen Fork — Design Brief (synthesis of 7 research tracks)**

WHAT: A static, GitHub-Pages-deployable, fully client-side braille asset generator: text -> verified braille (liblouis) -> STL (3D print), SVG (swell paper / laser / sign shops), and Unicode braille output — with a live, dual-audience preview. No competitor combines these: TouchSee is STL-only, brailletranslator.org is Unicode-only, BrailleBlaster is desktop BRF-only, the lone SVG tool is toy-grade. The fork can own the "braille asset generator" category.

FOR WHOM: (1) blind/low-vision users verifying braille on refreshable braille displays; (2) TVIs/teachers producing learning materials; (3) sighted makers and sign shops producing tactile output they cannot themselves read — whose #1 anxiety, named across every ecosystem signal, is "is this braille correct?"

WHY THESE CHOICES:
- **Correctness first.** The current app feeds UTF-8 bytes into liblouis's 16-bit widechar buffer, so Spanish/French — languages it advertises — produce mojibake dots; and dots 7/8 are dropped, so 8-dot tables emboss wrong. Wrong braille is inaccessible content regardless of WCAG score. Fix: JS strings are natively UTF-16 and the bundled liblouis.a is a UCS-2 build — marshal via stringToUTF16 (build-toolchain's zero-risk path wins over the UCS-4 recompile; revisit UCS-4 only on a from-source engine rebuild). Extend the cell matrix to 2x4 / 8 bits.
- **Two-stage engine.** 14.2 MB of the 26 MB monolith is embedded tables; one language needs ~50-300 KB. Relink the repo's EXISTING prebuilt liblouis.a (same clang-23 generation as current emsdk — inspected, low ABI risk) into a ~1 MB translator wasm running in a Worker. The app becomes fully useful (preview/SVG/copy) in seconds; the STL engine loads only on 3D intent. This dissolves defect #9 and unlocks the whole table catalog.
- **The preview IS the product's emotional core.** Render each wrapped plate line as (a) real Unicode braille text (U+2800-28FF passes 1:1 to refreshable braille displays via braille-patterns.cti — the killer verification feature no tool has) paired with (b) its source text for speech users, plus (c) an aria-hidden visual SVG dot grid sharing the exact layout engine as STL/SVG exports, so the preview is a faithful proof of the physical object.
- **Standards, not magic numbers.** The current constants are a lucky BANA/ADA hybrid. Replace with named presets (ADA, California CBC, BANA/LoC, Marburg/UKAAF, Jumbo) + hard clamps + cross-parameter guards, defaults biased for FDM undershoot (0.7 mm dot height, 2 mm plate). Live "this satisfies: ADA §703.3.1" labeling is itself a teaching feature.
- **Accessibility as identity.** Every competitor scanned fails basic a11y — ironic for the audience. WCAG 2.2 AA floor with cheap AAA wins, tested on real braille displays, is both table stakes and the strongest differentiator.

STL geometry path: timeboxed spike a ~300-line pure-JS plate+dome mesh generator (geometry is parametrically trivial); if mesh-parity passes, the 26 MB engine is deleted entirely and total app weight drops under 3 MB. Fallback: relink a modified main.cpp (accepting pre-translated Unicode braille, tables stripped) against the prebuilt OCCT .a — verified same-toolchain-generation, 1-2h work.

prioritized_features.name: UTF-16 input marshalling fix (kills the mojibake defect)
prioritized_features.rationale: Root defect: UTF-8 bytes widened per-byte into UCS-2 widechars (with sign-extension making it worse). JS strings are UTF-16; the bundled liblouis.a is a UCS-2 build — malloc + stringToUTF16 + pass widechar* is the zero-build-risk fix (build-toolchain wins over braille-translation's UCS-4 recompile for v1; UCS-4 deferred to any future from-source engine rebuild). Gate: 'niño' es-g1 must yield U+281D U+280A U+283B U+2815.

prioritized_features.name: Two-stage engine: ~1 MB liblouis-only translator wasm in a Worker, STL engine deferred until 3D intent
prioritized_features.rationale: Relink the repo's existing prebuilt C-only liblouis.a with current emsdk (same clang-23 generation, inspected via wasm producers section — low ABI risk, no autotools/WSL). App useful in seconds instead of after 26 MB; fixes defect #9; enables everything downstream. Embed only the 524 KB include-closure of the default tables.

prioritized_features.name: Translation robustness: mode=196 (dotsIO|ucBrl|noUndefined), partial-translation growth loop, dropped-char warning
prioritized_features.rationale: Empirically verified: mode 196 guarantees clean U+2800-28FF with no display-table prepend (side taken vs keeping braille-patterns.cti — mode flags are immune to double-inclusion). lou_translateString returns 1 even on truncation (documented trap) — check returned *inlen and grow. noUndefined drops chars SILENTLY: the UI must announce 'N characters could not be translated' — silent omission in a tactile medium is a correctness hazard.

prioritized_features.name: 8-dot support end-to-end (2x4 cell, bits 0-7, taller line pitch)
prioritized_features.rationale: getBrailleMatrix reads only bits 0-5; comp8 capitals ARE dot 7 (en-us-comp8 'H' = dots 1257), so 8-dot tables currently emboss wrong. Architect the shared cell renderer around an 8-bit mask so the defect class cannot recur; line pitch derived from cell height + gap (one formula for 6- and 8-dot).

prioritized_features.name: Dual-audience braille preview (the verification surface)
prioritized_features.rationale: One element per wrapped plate line (U+2800 is not whitespace — browsers won't wrap it; explicit lines also mirror the STL wrap exactly): real Unicode braille text node (NEVER aria-hidden — braille displays render it 1:1) + paired source text for speech users + aria-hidden visual SVG dots. Region headed 'Braille preview — N lines, M cells' for skippability. Directly resolves defect #8 and the ecosystem's #1 anxiety.

prioritized_features.name: STL path fix: engine accepts pre-translated Unicode braille (pure-JS spike gate, OCCT relink fallback)
prioritized_features.rationale: The STL wasm should not translate at all — stage 1 already produced the braille; stripping liblouis+tables shrinks it ~13 MB and fixes mojibake+8-dot in the 3D output. Decision gate: timeboxed pure-JS plate+spherical-cap mesh spike with mesh-diff parity vs upstream STLs; if it passes, the 26 MB engine and all its loading UX are deleted. Fallback: relink modified main.cpp vs prebuilt OCCT .a (same toolchain generation; keep emulated JS-EH, never -fwasm-exceptions; golden-STL regression test).

prioritized_features.name: mm-native accessible SVG export, Fill mode
prioritized_features.rationale: width/height in mm + matching viewBox (1 unit = 1 mm) — kills the 72/96-dpi error class in Inkscape/Illustrator/LightBurn/Cricut. Filled #000 circles (swell paper/UV/print). role=img + <title>/<desc> (desc carries the Unicode braille string, table, preset, dimensions) + aria-labelledby — the exported file is itself braille-display-readable; no existing tool does this. Geometry only, never a braille font. Thin renderer over the SAME layout engine as STL.

prioritized_features.name: Dimensional presets + clamps + FDM-honest defaults
prioritized_features.rationale: Named presets with exact standard numbers (see braille_specs), Custom mode live-labeling which standards current values satisfy. Hard clamps + cross-parameter guards (merged-dot and cell-ambiguity prevention). Raise defaults: dot height 0.6→0.7 mm (FDM prints 0.5-designed as 0.38 measured — the current default lands below ADA floor in reality), plate 1→2 mm. Store line pitch directly (current formula wrongly bakes dot diameter into it — presets must round-trip).

prioritized_features.name: Curated ~22-language table dropdown with human names
prioritized_features.rationale: Replace 5 raw-filename options with the verified curated list (grouped, labeled from #-display-name metadata, grade/8-dot variants marked, en-ueb-g2 default). Caveats honored: verify el.ctb on the shipped engine; label ja-kantenji honestly (kanji braille, not mainstream kana tenji); no Vietnamese/Thai in 3.36.

prioritized_features.name: WCAG 2.2 AA structural rebuild (pages not tabs, focus, live regions, labels, contrast, forced-colors, reduced-motion)
prioritized_features.rationale: All three UI researchers converge: dissolve the fake tabs into real pages (Docs = native HTML, killing the 800px iframe), delete outline:none, pre-provisioned role=status/role=alert singletons, fieldset/legend groups, inputmode=decimal text fields with explicit errors (never silent clamping), ≥24px targets, dual-theme OKLCH tokens, forced-colors + prefers-reduced-motion support, never-disabled Generate. See a11y_checklist.

prioritized_features.name: Translation + geometry regression test suite (golden vectors in CI)
prioritized_features.rationale: The empirical vectors (see test_cases) are regression armor for any engine/table upgrade — version coupling is proven breaking in both directions (3.36 'base' opcode fails on 3.2; el.ctb fails on 3.38). Plus golden-STL byte/mesh comparison for the geometry path.

prioritized_features.name: BRF export (embosser-ready)
prioritized_features.rationale: Days not weeks: map Unicode braille through the verified 64-char NABCC string, wrap 40 cells x 25 lines, CRLF + form-feed. Serves TVIs/embosser owners; matches the free-web baseline (brailletranslators.com) and BrailleBlaster interop. 6-dot only — grey out for comp8 tables.

prioritized_features.name: Back-translation round-trip check in the preview
prioritized_features.rationale: lou_backTranslateString is native and auto-recognizes Unicode braille: 'this braille reads back as: ...' directly answers the wrong-braille-on-permanent-signage fear. Cheap once the translator wasm exists.

prioritized_features.name: SVG Cut/Drill mode + mirror + named layers (sign-shop workflow)
prioritized_features.rationale: Raster-braille drill patterns (stroke-only #FF0000 circles at bead-hole diameter — a SEPARATE parameter from visual dot diameter) are the #1 named pain locked inside $$$ engraving suites. Mirror = baked flipped coordinates (never a transform attribute — CAM importers mishandle them). Layer groups with pure-RGB colors for LightBurn palette matching. High differentiator, but deferrable past the core ship.

prioritized_features.name: Lazy table fetch via build-time dependency manifest (expanded catalog)
prioritized_features.rationale: liblouis resolves 'include' synchronously from FS — the manifest must pre-write the full closure into MEMFS before translate (resolver script already written). ~1.5 MB for a no-CJK expanded set; CJK on demand. Unlocks up to all 461 tables at KB-scale cost each.

prioritized_features.name: Copy braille / .txt download / dot-numbers alternate view
prioritized_features.rationale: Serves braille-display users, embosser workflows, TVI teaching, and speech users on pre-2023.2 NVDA (which silently skipped U+28xx). Small surface once the preview exists.

prioritized_features.name: PWA: manifest + hand-rolled service worker, offline engines, consent-based update toast
prioritized_features.rationale: Teachers/transcribers on school networks are a real audience. Cache-first hashed engines, navigator.storage.persist(), explicit 'download engine for offline' control. GH Pages 10-min max-age means the SW must own caching.

prioritized_features.name: Settings persistence + share links + keyboard shortcuts + download toasts
prioritized_features.rationale: localStorage settings with versioned key + reset (3.3.7 Redundant Entry); share state in URL hash (out of referrers); modifier-only shortcuts (2.1.4); named download links with focus move.

prioritized_features.name: CI accessibility + performance gates
prioritized_features.rationale: axe-core/Playwright sweeps (both themes, 320px reflow, forced-colors, reduced-motion), keyboard-only walk of the core flow, Lighthouse budgets (a11y=100, initial <100 KB gz), plus per-release manual NVDA/VoiceOver and one refreshable-braille-display pass.

prioritized_features.name: Interline proof sheet + shadow dots + calibration bar + print stylesheet
prioritized_features.rationale: Duxbury's marquee TVI proofing feature (print text above each braille line) is cheap once SVG layout exists; SimBraille shadow-dot convention on preview (off in exports); 20 mm scale bar + @media print for exact-scale swell-paper PDFs.

prioritized_features.name: 3D STL preview via lazy three.js (~190 KB gz) behind a disclosure
prioritized_features.rationale: Progressive enhancement only — canvas is a11y-opaque; SVG preview stays canonical. role=img + keyboard rotate/zoom buttons (2.5.7), no auto-rotate under reduced-motion.

prioritized_features.name: PEF + DXF exports, PNG with pHYs chunk
prioritized_features.rationale: PEF covers international embossers (RoboBraille world); DXF for engraver CAMs preferring it; PNG physical-size chunk (~30 lines) for raster consumers. All reuse the same layout engine; wait for demand.

prioritized_features.name: Batch labels / multi-label plates
prioritized_features.rationale: TouchSee caps at 15 labels; match later with per-label list input and common presets (nameplate, jar lid). Core single-plate flow first.

prioritized_features.name: Contraction lookup / positional highlighting via outputPos/inputPos
prioritized_features.rationale: lou_translate's position arrays give char<->cell mapping: hover/focus a cell to see which print characters produced it — turns the preview into a braille-learning aid (abcbraille proves demand). Also enables input-word-boundary BRF wrapping.

prioritized_features.name: UEB emphasis via typeform arrays
prioritized_features.rationale: italic/bold/underline -> UEB emphasis indicators; needs rich-input UI (markdown-ish); natural later upgrade.

a11y_checklist: Global :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid token; outline-offset: 2px } with >=3:1 contrast; delete every outline:none — SC 2.4.7 (AA), 2.4.13 (AAA, near-free at this size), 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (AA); use outline not box-shadow so it survives forced-colors

Two pre-provisioned singleton live regions in initial DOM: <div role='status'> (polite/atomic) for 'Generating…'/'STL ready'/'Preview updated', <div role='alert'> for failures; inject/replace text, never create regions on demand, <~120 chars — SC 4.1.3 (AA)

Dissolve fake tabs: Generator/Docs/License as separate pages with header/nav/main/footer landmarks, skip link, one h1, aria-current='page'; Console as <details> with role='log' — SC 1.3.1, 2.1.1, 4.1.2, 2.4.1, 2.4.8 (AAA free)
Replace the 800px-min-width Google Doc iframe with native semantic HTML docs — SC 1.4.10 Reflow at 320 CSS px (AA), 2.4.2

Braille preview: one DOM element per wrapped plate line; the Unicode braille (U+2800-28FF) as a REAL text node, NEVER aria-hidden (aria-hidden removes content from braille displays too); paired source-text per line for speech users; region heading 'Braille preview — N lines, M cells' for skippability — SC 1.1.1, 1.3.1

aria-hidden only on the decorative visual dot GRAPHICS (SVG grid); if a standalone SVG line has no text sibling, role='img' + aria-label='Braille: {source line}'; never expose hundreds of <circle> nodes to the AT tree
All form fields: <label for> with unit in the visible label ('Dot height (mm)'); accessible name contains visible text — SC 2.5.3, 3.3.2, 2.4.6

Dimension fields: <input type='text' inputmode='decimal'> (GOV.UK pattern, not type=number); validate with explicit messages ('Dot height must be between 0.3 and 1.0 mm'), never silent clamping; aria-invalid + aria-describedby inline errors + focus to first invalid — SC 3.3.1 (A), 3.3.3 (AA), 2.4.3
fieldset+legend for grade radios and plate-dimension cluster (most reliably announced grouping across speech AND braille displays) — SC 1.3.1
Targets >=24x24 CSS px everywhere; Generate/Download >=44x44 — SC 2.5.8 (AA), 2.5.5 (AAA)

Dual-theme OKLCH token system: body text >=4.5:1 (aim 7:1 for 1.4.6 AAA), large text >=3:1, non-text UI boundaries + preview dots vs plate >=3:1, never color-only state — SC 1.4.3, 1.4.11, 1.4.1; rem-based sizing surviving 200% text resize and text-spacing overrides — SC 1.4.4, 1.4.12

Forced-colors (Windows Contrast Themes): SVG dot fills = currentColor/CanvasText (forced-colors does NOT touch SVG fills), selected state via border/underline shape, real borders on buttons, focus via outline — supports 1.4.1/1.4.11 under user palettes
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): all non-essential animation off, no auto-rotate, static progress text — SC 2.3.3 (AAA), 2.2.2 (A)

Engine loading: app shell interactive immediately; labelled native <progress> ('Loading braille engine…'); bar updates continuously but SPEAK milestones only (25/50/75/ready) via role=status; aria-busy on gated section — SC 4.1.3, 1.3.1

Never disable Generate: validate on activation and announce specific errors, or queue the job ('generating as soon as engine is ready'); any truly disabled control uses aria-disabled='true' styled >=3:1 (the current 1.9:1 is exempt from 1.4.3 but a real low-vision barrier)

Download flow: inject persistent <a download> named with filename + size ('Download STL — hello-world_ueb-g2_0.7mm.stl, 245 KB'), announce via role=status, MOVE FOCUS to the link, never auto-navigate — SC 4.1.3, 2.4.3, 2.4.4

Exported SVGs: role='img' + <title id> + <desc id> (desc carries the Unicode braille string, table, preset, mm dimensions) + aria-labelledby='titleId descId' — the only reliably-announced SVG pattern (2024 NVDA/JAWS testing)
Fully keyboard-operable, no traps, no drag-only interactions (3D preview gets rotate/zoom/reset buttons) — SC 2.1.1, 2.1.2, 2.1.3 (AAA achievable), 2.5.7 (AA)
Preview braille font stack for the Unicode string (Apple Braille, Segoe UI Symbol, Noto Sans Symbols 2, DejaVu) so sighted users don't see tofu; visual dots rendered as SVG for mm fidelity
html lang='en'; lang='es'/'fr'/etc. on echoed source-text nodes when a non-English table is selected — SC 3.1.1, 3.1.2 (AA)
Persist settings (table, dimensions, theme, preview mode) with visible 'Reset to defaults' — SC 3.3.7; Help/Docs link in consistent location — SC 3.2.6; unique <title> per page — SC 2.4.2
Modifier-only keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl/Cmd+Enter generate) with aria-keyshortcuts + '?' help dialog — SC 2.1.4

AT test matrix as release gate: axe-core CI + manual NVDA+Chrome/Firefox, JAWS, VoiceOver (macOS/iOS), TalkBack, keyboard-only pass, 400% zoom/320px, Windows Contrast Themes, voice control, and one refreshable-braille-display pass (or NVDA Braille Viewer) confirming literal expected cells; document JAWS/VoiceOver U+28xx speech behavior on first pass (not publicly documented)
visual_direction:
**"Tactile Modernism" — precision instrument with warmth.** The UI borrows the language of embossed paper and the braille cell itself; the braille preview panel is the hero. Explicitly rejected: glassmorphism (blur/translucency is a contrast liability + GPU cost) and full neo-brutalism (tone mismatch for a trustworthy assistive instrument — keep only its strong-border instinct).

- **Motif**: 2x3/2x4 dot-cell as logo/favicon; subtle low-contrast dot-grid background texture (removed under forced-colors); dots as bullets and progress markers.
- **Surfaces**: paper-flat with 1.5-2px borders on interactive elements (borders survive Windows High Contrast; heavy shadows don't) + soft dual 'emboss' shadows for elevation; radii 8-12px; generous whitespace.
- **Color**: all tokens OKLCH via light-dark() with color-scheme, 3-way auto/light/dark toggle (data-theme attr, pre-paint inline script, persisted). Light: warm paper bg oklch(.97 .005 90), text ~13:1. Dark: soft charcoal oklch(~.18) (not pure black — halation), text ~15:1. One accent: cobalt-indigo oklch(.55 .18 265) light / oklch(.75 .13 265) dark, reserved for primary action, links, focus ring, raised dots. prefers-contrast:more overrides thicken borders and push toward 7:1.
- **Type**: self-hosted Atkinson Hyperlegible Next variable (the Braille Institute's own 2025 typeface — the brand story AND a low-vision legibility win; covers latin-ext for es/fr) + Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for console/tabular readouts (tabular-nums). Fluid clamp() scale, base 16-18px, line-height 1.5-1.6, measure <=70ch. Never render visual braille with fonts — SVG dots only for mm fidelity.
- **Layout**: 4px spacing grid; single-column task order (input -> options -> generate -> status -> preview -> downloads) that IS the DOM order; live counters near input ('Cells 42 · Lines 3 · Plate 148 x 76 mm') as plain text, not live regions.
- **Motion**: tokens 120/200/320ms, transform/opacity only; signature micro-moment = dots 'rise' into the preview (scale .6->1, ~12ms stagger, <400ms) evoking embossing; everything off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- **Trust row footer**: version SHA, engine version, 'works offline' state, AGPL source link.
build_architecture:
**Zero-build vanilla + two-stage wasm, on GitHub Pages' actual constraints.**

Stack: semantic HTML + modern CSS (@layer, OKLCH, light-dark(), container queries — all Baseline) + ES modules with an import map; no framework, no bundler (tripwire: adopt Preact+htm via import map only if the UI grows past ~3 complex views). Vendored deps only (offline/PWA/supply-chain). Type safety via JSDoc + //@ts-check + tsc --noEmit in CI; ESLint, html-validate, axe/Playwright, Lighthouse budgets in CI. Deploy via actions/deploy-pages; a small Action injects the commit SHA, gzips engines, emits sizes.json + the table dependency manifest. Meta CSP: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'.

Pages constraints that shape everything: no custom headers -> no COOP/COEP -> NO SharedArrayBuffer/pthreads (all wasm single-threaded; plain Workers fine); application/wasm NOT in Fastly's compressed types -> big engines ship as self-compressed .wasm.gz inflated via DecompressionStream (Baseline all engines) with a byte-accurate <progress> (identity encoding keeps Content-Length truthful), preserving instantiateStreaming.

**Stage 0** (<60 KB): full UI interactive immediately. **Stage 1** (~1 MB raw / ~350 KB gz): liblouis-only translator wasm in a Worker — relinked from the repo's EXISTING prebuilt liblouis.a (verified clang-23 generation = current emsdk 6.0.x; C-only ABI ≈ nil risk; one emcc command, no autotools: -Oz -flto, MODULARIZE, EXPORT_ES6, ALLOW_MEMORY_GROWTH, FILESYSTEM on, exports lou_translateString/lou_backTranslateString/malloc/free + ccall/FS/stringToUTF16/UTF16ToString) with the 524 KB default-table include-closure embedded; expanded languages lazy-fetched per build-time dependency manifest and FS.writeFile'd into MEMFS under LOUIS_TABLEPATH before translate (liblouis resolves includes synchronously — full closure must be pre-written). Enables as-you-type preview + SVG + BRF + copy. **Stage 2** (STL): DECISION GATE — timeboxed pure-JS mesh spike (plate + spherical-cap dots + ~50-line binary STL writer; mesh-diff parity vs upstream across parameter ranges, manifold checks in a slicer). PASS -> no big engine at all, app <3 MB total. FAIL -> relink modified main.cpp (accepts pre-translated UTF-16 Unicode braille; liblouis + 13 MB tables stripped; 8-dot matrix) against the prebuilt OCCT .a with current emsdk — keep upstream flags, STACK_SIZE=5242880, default emulated JS-EH (the .a uses invoke_ wrappers; never -fwasm-exceptions); golden-STL regression; pin an emsdk whose LLVM hash neighbors 358db292 only if symbols fail. Load on explicit 3D intent + optional prefetch gated on saveData/effectiveType.

Both engines in Workers (postMessage with request ids, transferable ArrayBuffers); main thread stays idle. One shared layout engine (translate -> wrap at blank cells -> cell grid -> dot centers) feeds preview, SVG, STL, and BRF so every output is provably the same object. PWA: manifest + ~120-line hand-rolled SW (shell precache keyed by SHA; engines/tables cache-first by content-hashed filename; update toast with user-consent skipWaiting; navigator.storage.persist()). Fallback everywhere: the fork can ship stage 1 with the UNTOUCHED upstream 26 MB index.wasm lazy-loaded for STL while the geometry decision plays out.
braille_specs:
## Dimensional presets (all mm: dot base diameter / dot height / in-cell dot pitch / cell-to-cell pitch / line-to-line pitch)

| Preset | Dia | Height | Dot pitch | Cell pitch | Line pitch | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **ADA signage (US)** — default for signs | 1.5 | 0.7 | 2.4 | 6.2 | 10.1 | Mid-range of ADA 2010 Table 703.3.1 (dia 1.5–1.6, h 0.6–0.9, dot 2.3–2.5, cell 6.1–7.6, line 10.0–10.2); height biased up for FDM |
| **California CBC (Title 24)** — "works everywhere in US" | 1.6 | 0.7 | 2.5 | 7.6 | 10.2 | CBC 11B-703.3.1 pins ADA maxima (0.100/0.300/0.400 in); ADA preset is NOT auto-CA-compliant |
| **BANA / Library of Congress Spec 800** (paper feel; app's current lineage) | 1.44 | 0.48 | 2.34 | 6.2 | 10.16 | brailleauthority.org "Size and Spacing of Braille Characters" |
| **Marburg Medium / UKAAF (Europe)** | 1.6 | 0.5 | 2.5 | 6.0 | 10.0 | UKAAF B008 (h 0.5±0.1, dia 1.5±0.25) + Marburg spacing; = Australian Braille Authority |
| **Jumbo (learning / reduced sensitivity)** | 1.6 | 0.8 | 3.1 | 9.4 | 15.0 | Perkins Jumbo Brailler / RNIB geometry; line = ISO 17049 ceiling |

**Hard clamps** (union of standards + FDM practice): dia 1.0–2.0 · height 0.3–1.0 · dot pitch 2.0–3.2 · cell pitch 5.1–9.5 · line pitch 10.0–20.6 (ceiling admits BANA double spacing ≈ 20 mm for beginners) · plate ≥1.0 (default 2.0). ISO 17049 legal envelope for reference: a 2.2–2.8, b 2.0–2.8, p 5.1–6.8, q 10.0–15.0, d 1.0–1.7, h 0.3–0.7 (h>0.5 outdoors).
**Cross-parameter guards**: dotPitch ≥ dia + 0.3 (dome bases merge otherwise) · (cellPitch − dotPitch) ≥ dotPitch (tactile cell segmentation) · store line pitch DIRECTLY (never derive from dot diameter — current formula is nonstandard and breaks preset round-trips); for 8-dot, cell height grows one dot pitch and line pitch derives as cellHeight + gap.
**Soft warnings**: h<0.5 (ISO outdoor floor) · h>0.9 (exceeds all standards) · >40 cells/line · <6 mm blank margin (ISO exclusion zone).
**Dot profile**: spherical-cap dome only (optionally dome-on-frustum) — ADA "domed or rounded", ISO "not flat or pointed"; never cone/flat-top. **FDM defaults**: height 0.7 (0.5-designed prints as 0.38 measured — ASTRJ study), optional explicit "+0.1 mm FDM compensation" toggle; docs note 0.1–0.15 mm layers and CHI 2024 finding that 75–90° (stand-up) orientation reads best. **No pharma preset** (ISO 17351's 0.20 mm carton emboss is meaningless in rigid plastic — document why). **SVG cut/drill hole diameter is a separate parameter** (default 1.6 mm ≈ 1/16 in raster bead), decoupled from visual dot diameter.
risks: Silent liblouis traps: lou_translateString returns 1 even on truncated output (only signal = returned *inlen), and noUndefined drops untranslatable chars with NO output — both must be paired with explicit checks/warnings or the app ships wrong tactile content while looking green

Engine<->table version coupling is proven breaking BOTH directions (3.36 'base' opcode fails on 3.2 engine; el.ctb Greek fails on the 3.38 parser) — tables must be pinned to the exact shipped engine release, with the golden-vector suite re-run on any upgrade; verify el.ctb on the shipped engine before listing Greek

ABI risk on the OCCT relink: emscripten officially guarantees NO cross-version ABI compatibility; mitigated (same clang-23 generation verified via wasm producers sections, emulated-EH flags matched) but the golden-STL test and emsdk-pinning fallback are mandatory, and -fwasm-exceptions must never be added
Pure-JS geometry spike may fail slicer-manifold/parity checks (dot profile curvature, base fusion) — that's why it's a timeboxed gate with the OCCT relink as fallback, not a bet the plan depends on

JAWS and VoiceOver per-character speech behavior for U+2800-28FF is NOT publicly documented — must be manually tested in the first AT pass before shipping the preview messaging; NVDA pre-2023.2 silently skips braille chars (dot-numbers alternate view is the mitigation)

FDM undershoot means 'standard-compliant' exported geometry can PRINT out of spec (0.5 designed -> 0.38 measured) — the compensation toggle must keep nominal-vs-exported values honest or the compliance labels become misleading

GitHub Pages constraints are load-bearing: no custom headers (no COOP/COEP -> single-threaded wasm forever on this host), no wasm gzip (self-.gz + DecompressionStream required), 10-min cache max-age (service worker must own caching); any host migration re-opens these decisions

Scope creep is the #1 delivery risk: the research surfaced ~6 'unique differentiators' (drill-mode SVG, interline proofs, back-translation, BRF/PEF, batch, learning tools) — the must tier is deliberately correctness+preview+SVG+a11y; everything else waits

Competitive claims partially unverified: TouchSee features were triangulated while its site refused connections, and Thingiverse listings couldn't be fetched — hands-on re-check before any public comparison copy
AGPL-3.0 obligations follow the fork: all source (including build tooling for the wasm artifacts) must stay published; fine for a GitHub-Pages app but worth stating in the README
Safari may evict PWA storage after ~7 days of disuse for non-installed sites — navigator.storage.persist() + install guidance mitigate but offline promises should be worded carefully
The 16-bit UCS-2 choice leaves astral-plane input (emoji) as surrogate-pair edge cases — strip-or-warn on input; revisit --enable-ucs4 only when/if the engine is rebuilt from source
